subject.title: Multi-agent orchestration is unstable: concurrent agents add/config overwrites, session-lock failures, and detached child work

question: Should this issue remain the canonical umbrella while focused fixes land, or should maintainers replace it with narrower canonical issues for session-lock ownership, durable completion delivery, fallback lanes, and cancellation semantics?
rationale: The bug is valid, but the solution boundary spans core session ownership, message delivery guarantees, provider failover behavior, and detached child cleanup, which automation should not choose as one architecture direction.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Land Focused Fixes
options.body: Keep this issue open, require focused PRs or issues for each root cause, and close the umbrella only when the linked symptoms are fixed or explicitly split.

options.title: Promote Completion Isolation Design
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96975 the canonical product direction for the completion-isolation piece and link the remaining bug reports to separate owners.

options.title: Split By Failure Mode
options.body: Select one canonical issue each for config writes, session locks, subagent delivery, auth failover, and detached work, then close this umbrella after preserving the production evidence links.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Land Focused Fixes
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, require focused PRs or issues for each root cause, and close the umbrella only when the linked symptoms are fixed or explicitly split.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily an OpenClaw architecture/product boundary choice and steipete is the strongest available routing signal from VISION-level guidance and subagent registry history.
